# LLM Radar

> The full LLM landscape in one auto-updated dashboard: hosted models (pricing &
> context) and open-weights models (adoption & licenses). Independent, open-source,
> refreshed daily. By Ronald Mego — https://ronaldmego.github.io/llm-radar

LLM Radar consolidates the large-language-model market into a single continuously
updated view, split into two catalogs. It is an independent project, not affiliated
with OpenRouter or Hugging Face.

## What it tracks

- Hosted models (commercial, API-called): source OpenRouter public `/api/v1/models`.
  Fields: model name, provider, context window (K tokens), price per 1M input tokens,
  price per 1M output tokens, modalities, release date.
- Open-weights models (self-hostable): source Hugging Face Hub public model listing.
  Fields: model name, org, type, 30-day downloads, community likes, license, gated
  status, release date. The universe covers text, multimodal (image-text-to-text)
  and vision/OCR (image-to-text) models, and is built from two rankings per type —
  30-day downloads (established adoption) and the Hub trending signal (what landed
  this week) — so a release published days ago is present, not just what is already
  popular.

## Definitions

- Context window (K): max tokens (prompt + response) per call, in thousands.
- $/1M in, $/1M out: US dollars per one million input / output tokens.
- Permissive license: open license (Apache-2.0, MIT, etc.) allowing commercial use
  and redistribution without acceptance gates.
- Gated model: open-weights model whose download requires accepting terms.
- Cheapest capable: lowest input price among models with >=100K context.
- Type: what a model can be fed. Hosted side, from OpenRouter input modalities (text
  only / image / document + image / audio+video); open-weights side, from the Hub
  pipeline tag (text / multimodal / vision-OCR). Read from the API, never hand-assigned.
- Just landed: models published in the last 45 days, ranked by likes. Ranking recent
  arrivals by downloads returns nothing — the 30-day counter has not moved yet.
- Third-party quantization: a repackaging of someone else's weights (GGUF, AWQ, MLX,
  4-bit). Kept in the catalog, excluded from charts and ranked tables.
- Open weights available (hosted): the hosted model has a published Hugging Face
  repository, so the same weights can be self-hosted.

## Method

OpenRouter API + Hugging Face API -> Python (pandas, great-tables, plotly) -> Quarto ->
GitHub Pages, refreshed daily by GitHub Actions. Zero server, no API key. Fully
open-source: https://github.com/ronaldmego/llm-radar

## How to cite

LLM Radar — the full LLM landscape (hosted pricing & context plus open-weights
adoption & licenses), by Ronald Mego. https://ronaldmego.github.io/llm-radar
